\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{শর্ত} (shôrtô)}{শর্ত (shôrtô)}]{\bn{শর্ত} (shôrtô) — a condition; a term (of an agreement)}

\label{lesson:BN-C368-shorto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for an expectation, then the Bengali for the future.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{শর্ত}}
\textbf{\bn{শর্ত}} — \emph{shôrtô} — \textquotedblleft{}a condition; a term (of an agreement)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আমার} \bn{একটা} \bn{শর্ত} \bn{আছে}: \bn{তুমি} \bn{যদি} \bn{আসো}, \bn{তাহলে} \bn{আমিও} \bn{যাব।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āmār ekṭā shôrtô āchhe: tumi jôdi āso, tāhôle āmio jābô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I have one condition: if you come, I'll go too.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{শর্ত}} (\emph{shôrtô}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{sharṭ}, a condition, through Persian: the 'if' a deal depends on.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shôrtô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shôrtô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āmār ekṭā shôrtô āchhe: tumi jôdi āso, tāhôle āmio jābô.} — I have one condition: if you come, I'll go too.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for an expectation, then the Bengali for the future, then say \emph{shôrtô} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{শর্ত} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A condition; a term (of an agreement)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{অবস্থা} (ôbôsthā)}{অবস্থা (ôbôsthā)}]{\bn{অবস্থা} (ôbôsthā) — a state; a condition (of something)}

\label{lesson:BN-C368-obostha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for the future, then the Bengali for a condition.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{অবস্থা}}
\textbf{\bn{অবস্থা}} — \emph{ôbôsthā} — \textquotedblleft{}a state; a condition (of something)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{রাস্তার} \bn{অবস্থা} \bn{খারাপ} \bn{হলে} \bn{আমরা} \bn{বাসে} \bn{যাব} \bn{না।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rāstār ôbôsthā khārāp hôle āmrā bāse jābô nā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the roads are in a bad state, we won't go by bus.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{অবস্থা}} (\emph{ôbôsthā}) is Sanskrit \emph{avasthā}, a state or condition (Monier-Williams): how a thing or a person is at present.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôbôsthā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôbôsthā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rāstār ôbôsthā khārāp hôle āmrā bāse jābô nā.} — If the roads are in a bad state, we won't go by bus.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for the future, then the Bengali for a condition, then say \emph{ôbôsthā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{অবস্থা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A state; a condition (of something)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{পরিস্থিতি} (pôristhiti)}{পরিস্থিতি (pôristhiti)}]{\bn{পরিস্থিতি} (pôristhiti) — a situation; circumstances}

\label{lesson:BN-C368-poristhiti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a condition, then the Bengali for a state of things.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{পরিস্থিতি}}
\textbf{\bn{পরিস্থিতি}} — \emph{pôristhiti} — \textquotedblleft{}a situation; circumstances\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{পরিস্থিতি} \bn{বদলালে} \bn{আমাকে} \bn{ফোন} \bn{করো।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pôristhiti bôdlāle āmāke phon kôro.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Call me if the situation changes.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{পরিস্থিতি}} (\emph{pôristhiti}) is a modern learned compound of Sanskrit \emph{pari-}, around, and \emph{sthiti}, a standing or state (Monier-Williams): how things stand all around. The compound itself is not in the dictionary.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pôristhiti}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pôristhiti}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pôristhiti bôdlāle āmāke phon kôro.} — Call me if the situation changes.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a condition, then the Bengali for a state of things, then say \emph{pôristhiti} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{পরিস্থিতি} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A situation; circumstances\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{যতক্ষণ} (jôtôkkhôn)}{যতক্ষণ (jôtôkkhôn)}]{\bn{যতক্ষণ} (jôtôkkhôn) — as long as}

\label{lesson:BN-C368-jotokkhon}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a state of things, then the Bengali for a situation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{যতক্ষণ}}
\textbf{\bn{যতক্ষণ}} — \emph{jôtôkkhôn} — \textquotedblleft{}as long as\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ঝড়} \bn{না} \bn{থামলে} \bn{আমরা} \bn{যতক্ষণ} \bn{দরকার} \bn{এখানে} \bn{থাকব।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jhôṛ nā thāmle āmrā jôtôkkhôn dôrkār ekhāne thākbô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the storm doesn't stop, we'll stay here as long as we need to.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{যতক্ষণ}} (\emph{jôtôkkhôn}) is \bn{যত}, 'as much as', with Sanskrit \emph{kṣaṇa}, a moment (Monier-Williams): for as many moments as. It is often answered by \bn{ততক্ষণ}, 'for that long'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jôtôkkhôn}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jôtôkkhôn}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jhôṛ nā thāmle āmrā jôtôkkhôn dôrkār ekhāne thākbô.} — If the storm doesn't stop, we'll stay here as long as we need to.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a state of things, then the Bengali for a situation, then say \emph{jôtôkkhôn} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{যতক্ষণ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}As long as\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{অথবা} (ôthôbā)}{অথবা (ôthôbā)}]{\bn{অথবা} (ôthôbā) — or else; or otherwise}

\label{lesson:BN-C368-othoba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a situation, then the Bengali for as long as.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{অথবা}}
\textbf{\bn{অথবা}} — \emph{ôthôbā} — \textquotedblleft{}or else; or otherwise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{কাল} \bn{ছুটি} \bn{হলে} \bn{আমরা} \bn{সিনেমায়} \bn{যাব}, \bn{অথবা} \bn{বাড়িতে} \bn{থাকব।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāl chhuṭi hôle āmrā sinemāy jābô, ôthôbā bāṛite thākbô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If tomorrow is a holiday, we'll go to the cinema or else stay at home.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{অথবা}} (\emph{ôthôbā}) is Sanskrit \emph{athavā}, 'or' (Monier-Williams). It is more weighty than \bn{বা} and often offers a second plan.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôthôbā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôthôbā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāl chhuṭi hôle āmrā sinemāy jābô, ôthôbā bāṛite thākbô.} — If tomorrow is a holiday, we'll go to the cinema or else stay at home.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a situation, then the Bengali for as long as, then say \emph{ôthôbā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{অথবা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Or else; or otherwise\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
